c: Disco Deco is an aesthetic design prevalent from the mid-1960s to the 1970s and a design revival of 1920s Art Deco that is characterized by classic geometric glamour with the hedonistic, vibrant energy of the rising disco nightclub era, such as Studio 54. It often associates sleek symmetry with electric nightlife energy, along with this aesthetic focusing more likely on psychedelic elements but with a luxurious and disco-related appearance.
The aesthetic is defined by bright and psychedelic imagery evoking a sense of playfulness and glamor. Visuals include geometric blocky typography.

For the accessories, dramatic silhouettes incorporate ultra-wide leg trousers, halter neck silhouettes, expansive bell sleeves, and plunging necklines that catch the light with movement, featuring luxe statement pieces such as towering platform heels, oversized tinted sunglasses, metallic boots, and faux-fur stoles, along with sequins and lamé, that often focus on head-to-toe shimmer, platinum chainmail, heavily sequined jumpsuits and liquid-gold metallic sets.

Refracted lights include melting mirror sculptures to bounce ambient party light by night, natural light by day and hanging mirrored disco fixtures, featuring rich material color palettes such as smooth mohair, tinted, smoked glass, plush velvets, dark, glossy marble, and travertine, with elements that often focus on lightings, refracted sparkles dancing across dark, atmospheric rooms, colorful glass pendant lights and neon signs, along with geometric and fluid silhouettes that incorporate fan shapes, streamlined Art Deco chevrons, sunburst motifs diffused with the undulating, low-slung, modular seating popular in 70s lounges.

Statement furniture incorporates velvet-upholstered, curved sofas (such as the luxurious Kagan or Togo styles) associated with glossy, asymmetrical black coffee tables, featuring bold architecture such as the dramatic fluted wall paneling, moody paint colors (such as obsidian, rich burgundy or deep emerald) and arched doorways that make metallics pop, elements that focus on metallic and reflective surfaces, often leaning on polished brass, the ultimate stapled mirrored tiles, gold leaf, high-shine chrome, lacquer, and disco balls.
